newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Mark cross vols hold gains in busy Europe.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Mark cross vols hold gains in busy Europe.

text.p: Mark option volatilities were firm in Europe on Thursday, holding the bulk of overnight gains following the Bundesbank's rejection of Germany's plans to revalue its gold and other reserves.

Mark/French franc option implied volatility climbed to fresh highs amid the Buba/Bonn rift, extending gains already made this week on uncertainty over the outcome of Sunday's second round of voting in French parliamentary elections.
One-month mark/franc volatility stood at 3.3/3.8 percent at midsession in Europe, up from late Wednesday's 2.9/3.4 percent and 2.0/3.0 Monday.
"It's all risk premium over the uncertainty to EMU, first from the French elections and now from the reserve revaluation row in Germany," said a U.S. bank options trader in London.

Dealers said options trade had been hectic all week, predominantly in mark/franc and mark/lira options as spot rates were driven higher. The French franc tested four-month lows against the mark on Wednesday, dragging the lira to two-week lows in its wake.
One-month mark/lira volatility stood at 5.1/6.5 percent at the midsession, up from 4.5/5.0 Wednesday and 4.0/4.4 percent Monday.

Mark cross spot rates edged back in Europe today as the initial concerns over Buba criticism of the revaluation plans gave way to renewed expectations of a broad EMU start. The German government said on Wednesday it would stick with its plans despite the central bank's objections.
Dealers said some of the recent hefty risk premium may have been overdone. Current volatility levels looked extreme and were due for some retracement, they said.

"Selling a one-month 30 delta strangle gives you a break-even around 3.3500-3.4150 francs. It's incredibly unlikely to see either side of that range in one-month's time," said one options trader. "The French election risk has already been factored in, as well as the EMU risk, so the risk-reward is to the downside."
Selling a strangle entails selling a put and a call option of the same duration but at different strike prices.
Spot dollar/mark was firmer but off earlier highs as was dollar/yen. But the dollar has not strayed too far from recent ranges and volatilities and activity were relatively muted.
One-month dollar/mark stood at 9.6/9.9 percent, slightly up from 9.3/9.6 percent Wednesday. Dollar/yen one-month was trading at 11.2/11.7 percent against 11.4/11.9.
